Author: P.Naveen Rao Bench: P.Naveen Rao  HONOURABLE SRI JUSTICE P.NAVEEN RAO  WRIT PETITION NO.16596 of 2020  Date: 06.11.2020 Between:
Ghanshyam Das Karwa S/o.

Late Sri Harikishan Karwa, aged 52 years, occ: Business, R/o.14-7-392, Begumbazar,
Hyderabad.
 .....Petitioner

And The State of Telangana,
rep by its Principal Secretary,
Prohibition and Excise Department,
Secretariat, Hyderabad & others.

.....Respondents The Court made the following:
 2 PNRJ  WP 16596_2020  HONOURABLE SRI JUSTICE P.NAVEEN RAO  WRIT PETITION NO.16596 of 2020 ORDER:
Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned Government Pleader for Prohibition and Excise.
2. Petitioner is carrying on the business of jaggery and allied products in the name and style of M/s.Ramchander Laxminarayan Karwa at Begumbazar, Hyderabad.

He claims to have secured licence to do the business in jaggery from the Authority under the Food Safety and Standards Act,
2006 and he has been carrying the said business in strict compliance of statutory requirements.
He has several godowns to store the goods in which he is carrying on his business.

Petitioner alleges Ghanshyam Das Karwa vs State Of Telangana on 6 November, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70093787/
1 that on 16.05.2020, he was directed to open the godown in the premises bearing municipal No.14-6-38, Begumbazar, Hyderabad and forcibly took away 288 bags of black jaggery of 30 kgs each, total 8640 kgs, Navsagar powder of 1884.5 kgs and 120 kg Alum.

sentences.text: When stock was seized, no information was furnished to the petitioner on reasons for such seizure.

On further enquiry,
petitioner came to know that said stock was seized in connection with COR.No.70 of 2020 on the file of Prohibition and Excise Station, Deverkonda, based on confessional statement obtained from the accused therein.

This writ petition is filed seeking declaration of action of seizure of black jaggery as illegal, arbitrary and contrary to the principles of natural justice and to direct the 5th respondent to release the seized stock.
3. In counter affidavit, respondents contend that petitioner is indulging in manufacture of illicitly distilled liquor (I.D.liquor) and is involved in several crimes.

Having come to know that illegal manufacture and sale of I.D.liquor was going on in the house of Nenavath Raju, Uppugandi Thanda,
raid was conducted and huge 3 PNRJ WP 16596_2020 quantity of black jaggery, Navasagar powder and Alum were recovered.
Based on confession of the accused Nos 1 to 4, raid was conducted in the godwn of petitioner and huge quantity of black jaggery, Navasagar powder and Alum were seized.

According to respondents, COR.No.70 of 2020 was registered under Sections 7(A) read with Section 8(e) of A.P. Prohibition Act, 1995 and Section 34 (e) of A.P.Excise Act, 1968 and Section 3 (b) and 4(1) (111) of GUR (Regulation of Excise) Order, 1968 and investigation is pending.
It is further case of respondents that from out of seized stock from the godown of the petitioner, samples were collected and sent for chemical examination to the Chemical Examiner, Warangal.
The Chemical Examiner has tested the samples and opined that seized jaggery is not useful for human consumption, but it can be used as raw material in manufacturing illicit liquor.
4. According to learned counsel for petitioner, jaggery is an agricultural product and there is no prohibition on purchase, transport and sale of black jaggery.

On 22.12.2001, the Commissioner of Prohibition and Excise issued circular instructions directing the Law Enforcing Authorities not to harass business people, who were doing business in jaggery, as long as purchase is supported by bills and having valid transport documents.
According to learned counsel, jaggery was purchased in the State of Maharastra.
At the time of purchase, test reports were obtained showing the quality of jaggery as useful for human consumption and manufacturer has issued way bill.
Therefore, as it is validly purchased and transported, there is no bar in carrying on business in jaggery.

Merely because large quantity of jaggery is stored in the godown of petitioner, based on false confession,
respondents could not have seized the jaggery.
He further submits that jaggery is perishable item, if it is not released it will perish and petitioner would be subjected to huge financial loss for no fault of him.

Per contra, according to learned Government Pleader, material on record would disclose that petitioner is indulging in manufacture of illicit liquor and the fact that several crimes are registered against him would go to show that he is conniving in manufacturing illicit liquor for a long time.
He would submit that it was not necessary that traders should involve in actual manufacturing.

If excise officials have reasonable apprehension that huge quantity of jaggery and Alum are stored by a Ghanshyam Das Karwa vs State Of Telangana on 6 November, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70093787/
2 person, which is primarily intended to manufacture illicit liquor, it is permissible for the excise officials to seize the stock, so that they can prevent any further manufacturing of illicit liquor which is harmful for human consumption.

sentences.text: The crime is already registered and investigation is in progress.

He would further submit that as per the Chemical Analysis report, seized black jaggery is not useful for human consumption and therefore, balance of convenience is not in favour of petitioner to release the seized stock before investigation is completed and before confiscation proceedings are concluded.

In support of his contention, learned Government Pleader placed reliance on decision of Full Bench of this Court in Ganesh Traders (Kirana and General Merchants), Dhermapuri,
Karimnagar District v. District Collector, Karimnagar1 and decision of learned Judge of Common High Court in W.P.No.9471 of 2018.

Karimnagar District v. District Collector, Karimnagar1

sentences.text: 6. In this writ petition, limited grievance of petitioner is against seizure of black jaggery and not releasing the same.
It is not in dispute that COR. No.70 of 2020 was registered and petitioner is shown as one of the accused in the said crime.
The black jaggery was seized based on the confessional statement of accused Nos 1 to 4.

As investigation is in progress and confiscation proceedings are not taken-up so far, no opinion can be expressed on the alleged raid conducted on certain 2002 (1) ALD 210 (Full Bench) 5 PNRJ WP 16596_2020 houses, whether illicit liquor and huge quantity of jaggery and Alum were recovered, and whether there was valid confession leading to seizure of huge quantity of jaggery and Alum from the petitioner's godown and his involvement in the alleged offence.

Therefore, the only question for consideration is whether petitioner has made out case for grant of relief of declaration of action of respondents in seizing the black jaggery as illegal and arbitrary and direct them to release the same.
7. The excise officials apprehend that huge quantity of black jaggery is stored by the petitioner to use the same to produce illicit liquor.

They cite the history of involvement of petitioner in similar offences and rely on chemical examiner report to contend that the seized black jaggery is not fit for human consumption but can be used to produce illicit liquor.

On the scope of power of excise officials seizing black jaggery whenever they suspect that it is being used to produce illicit liquor need not detain this Court further having regard to the conclusions recorded in the majority opinion of the Full Bench in Ganesh Traders.

Paragraph No.52 reads as under:
"52.
We may now summarise our discussion on the main question whether keeping or being in possession of black jaggery material for the purpose of manufacture of liquor is an offence under the Excise Act.

(a) The provisions of the A. P. Excise Act including Sections 13(f) and 34(e) should be interpreted with reference to the objects of the Act and penal provisions dealing with excise offences should also receive broader interpretation having regard to the fact that the Excise Act is intended to achieve partially the objective of Article 47 of the Constitution of India;
(b) Having regard to the provisions of Sections 13, 34 and 53 and 55 of the Excise Act,
we must hold that if Commissioner, Collector, Police Officer or Excise Officer "has reason to believe" that black jaggery (material) is likely to be used for manufacture of Ghanshyam Das Karwa vs State Of Telangana on 6 November, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70093787/
3 ID liquor the same can be seized and persons can be arrested and subject to facts and circumstances of each case including any report of the chemical examiner a charge sheet can be filed under Section 34(e) of the Excise Act.

sentences.text:
(c) In a situation such as (a) and (b) above, if the circumstances so warrant the person/accused is entitled to approach under Section 482 of Cr.P.C.
and/or Article 226 of the Constitution of India and seek quashing of proceedings provided his case come within well settled principles for quashing F.I.R., charge sheet or criminal case.

However, a Writ Petition in such an event at the stage of investigation is not permissible when 6 PNRJ WP 16596_2020 there is prima facie material to show that black jaggery is not fit for human consumption and was intended for manufacture of ID liquor.

(d) As held by the Supreme Court in NASU SHEIKKS case (supra) if the F.I.R. shows the ingredients of offence under Section 34(e) read with Section 13(f) of the Excise Act, a person cannot be heard to say in High Court that he is carrying on business or transporting black jaggery either because he is an agriculturist or businessman.

All such pleas are to be raised before appropriate criminal Court."
[ Emphasis supplied]
8.

Thus, it can not be said that seizure was without power or jurisdiction nor it amounted to arbitrary exercise of power warranting interference of this Court even before the investigation is completed in COR.No.70 of 2020 and confiscation proceedings are taken to logical end.
Further having regard to the Chemical Examiner report, wherein report holds that seized black jaggery is not useful for human consumption, balance of convenience is also not in favour of petitioner.
As held by the Full Bench in Ganesh Traders, it is for the petitioner to work out remedies as available in law.
It is made clear that there is no expression of opinion on merits.
9. Accordingly, the writ petition is dismissed.
Pending miscellaneous petitions, if any, shall stand closed.
P.NAVEEN RAO,J 6th November, 2020 Nvl /tvk 7 PNRJ WP 16596_2020 HONOURABLE SRI JUSTICE P.NAVEEN RAO WRIT PETITION NO.16596 of 2020
